explanation: An elephant calf takes about 22 months to develop. A blue whale calf, far bigger, is born after 10 to 12 months, then grows fast on its mother's fat-rich milk.

claims.text: An African elephant's pregnancy lasts about 22 months.
A blue whale's pregnancy lasts about 10 to 12 months.
A newborn blue whale calf is far bigger than a newborn elephant calf.
Blue whale calves grow rapidly on their mother's very fat-rich milk.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: four listed; c1 and c2 hold numbers, so they are high. c3 and c4 are standard. The value for b is 11, the middle of the 10 to 12 months that the claim and the reveal show. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology, so none applies and every high-risk claim needs web evidence from checker A. rivalTest: 'the bigger animal must take longer' is the planted trap, which is why counterintuitive is set. Margin: sources give about 22 months for the African elephant and about 10 to 12 for the blue whale, so the answer holds under every figure on offer, and the ratio is about 2. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: both animals are known worldwide; months read the same everywhere. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 30 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a comparison item. doubts: the blue whale figure is less precisely known than the elephant's, so it is shown as a range; the answer holds at either end of it.
